post_title: Why my clothes are turning and glitching
post_details: Hello My clothes should look like this I already made white one and It works without any problem But when I made black one with same process, (Make patern on Illustrator and do same clo working process) My clothes start turning around models body and make wierd movement This is original pattern (I already used it when I make real clothes) (I know the seamline differences on 2D windows and I already changed and fixed it but It didnt make any differences) But when I start simulation,It makes wierd movement And start to turning around like this I checked every glitching spot, but I couldnt find any solution I want to know why and how to fix it Please give me the answer

comments.comment_body: It is hard to tell from afar, but from what I can discern the main issue seems to arise from this spot: Is it correct that you have two layers of pattern pieces overlaying each other? If yes, I think this part is colliding into itself. Best practice: - Initially build and simulate garments in the Default Fabric and only apply the final fabric after the garment is stable. - For standard-adult-sized garments, work in a particle distance of 20 until the garment is stable. - Build layers separately from one another and layer them over each other in an additional second step. - Pattern piece arrangement before simulation doesn't look symmetrically placed, which is working against the garment's favor when it comes to correct drape. - If there's indeed two layers on top of each other, when connecting them from edge to edge, set the Sewing Line Type to Turned so that they lie flat on top of each other instead of building up a puffy look. - You can also try strengthening the pattern pieces temporarily to see if the part I have circled in red might calm down and smooth itself out.

post_title: How to sew an inverted box pleat
post_details: Hi guys, would you be able to help me figure it out how to sew an inverted box pleat? The pleat is on a front panel of a skirt

comments.comment_body: Hi 26085454189593, It might be easier to arrange the pattern pieces in front of the avatar as they should be, then fold in the vent and see how the pieces should connect via the 3D Sewing tools. Either way, the lines should be connected as outlined in matching colors with the seamline notches pointing into the correct dimensions. Where you fold the vent in, the fold angle should be 0 (back side of fabric touching). The red seamlines will fall crisp with a fold angle of 360. Pink and green require Sewing Line Type to be set on Turned.

post_title: Performance and Rendering Issues on Mac: Seeking Advice for Hardware Configuration
post_details: Recently, I wanted to render a montage of 5 football jerseys. The render wasn't goodgrainy. I had to segment the renders and then assemble the images in Photoshop. I'll have many similar montages to create, and I often experience slowness in Clo3D. I'm using a Mac Mini M2 Pro, 16GB RAM, and an Apple Display 5k. I just read that the 5k screen could slow down the software. I'll consider lowering the screen resolution for the next use. This experience leads me to these questions: Would a computer configured for 3D provide much better results? Is the PC environment better suited for Clo3D? Ideally, I'd prefer to stay in an Apple environment with a Mac Studio, but I wouldn't hesitate to switch to a PC if it improves performance and render time. In the 3D world, apart from Clo (which I really like!), I'm now learning the Adobe Substance 3D suite. Thank you for shedding light on this matter.

comments.comment_body: Hi 10733584378265 For all the CLO3D Recommended Specs you can always look to this page HERE which is regularly updated with new information. Your RAM mentioned above is above the minimum, but below our recommended level. You also have not mentioned which OS you are currently using, but we always recommend updating to the latest. A computer that is configured and designed for 3D will usually perform the best. Many CLO users purchase high end gaming PCs with plenty of RAM and the newest graphics cards. But also when it comes to PC over MAC it is users preference. If you feel most comfortable in one that is always ok, but I can say that if you look more and more into 3D a PC does tend to be more commonly seen than a Mac
Thank you! Your guidance is helpful. I think I will make the switch to a PC... Best regards,
